dz.headline: Algeria targets 20,000 investment projects by 2029
dz.body: The government aims to realize 20,000 investment projects by 2029. The plan relies on a comprehensive census of available land.
dz.why: The land census is intended to provide the physical space necessary for businesses to establish these new operations.

dz.headline: Alger authorities revoke 12 transport operating licenses
dz.body: The Direction of Transport, Mobility, and Logistics withdrew 12 operating authorizations for transport lines in the capital. The move follows increased surveillance of the city's transport network.
dz.why: The removal of these licenses reduces the number of authorized operators permitted to run transport lines in Algiers.

dz.headline: Road accident in Djelfa injures 13 agricultural workers
dz.body: Thirteen agricultural workers were injured Wednesday afternoon in a road accident. The crash occurred on communal road No. 1 in Djelfa.
dz.why: The incident revealed the use of underage labor in the region.

dz.headline: SaÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¯dal restarts Hup Pharma plant in Constantine
dz.body: Public group SaÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¯dal has begun a gradual restart of production lines at the Hup Pharma unit. The site had been closed for three years.
dz.why: The reopening restores pharmaceutical production capacity in Constantine after a three-year hiatus.

dz.headline: Sonatrach nears LPG supply deal with Indian refiner
dz.body: Sonatrach is preparing to sign an agreement with India's largest refiner. The deal involves the monthly delivery of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).
dz.why: The agreement establishes a recurring monthly export stream of LPG from Algeria to the Indian energy market.

ao.headline: Angola expels 53,000 irregular foreigners in seven months
ao.body: Angolan police deported more than 53,000 foreign citizens in irregular situations over the last seven months. Commissioner Francisco Ribas announced the figure following a National Security Council meeting in Luanda. The operation targeted individuals involved in crimes including the illicit exploitation of diamonds.
ao.why: The crackdown targets foreign nationals engaged in the illegal extraction of diamonds to secure the country's mineral resources.

ao.why: The legal action seeks accountability for police and government officials following violence against opposition party members.

bj.why: The release ends the detention of a chronicler who had been convicted in a first-instance ruling on June 2, 2025.

bj.headline: Benin publishes health agent recruitment results
bj.body: Recruitment test results for health agents at departmental health directorates are available as of Thursday, Aug. 20. The lists of selected candidates are being posted.
bj.why: The availability of these lists determines which candidates will be hired to staff health structures.

bj.body: Minister of Sports and Civic Engagement BenoÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â®t Dato visited the Benin U20 women's national team on Tuesday, Aug. 18. The team is currently in a training camp in France.
bj.why: The visit occurs two weeks before the team competes in the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup Poland 2026.

bj.headline: Sounon Yico FC wins Banikoara football tournament
bj.body: Sounon Yico FC of Toura won the 6th edition of the Talent Football Vacances tournament on Sunday, Aug. 16. The final match took place at the Bani GansÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© stadium in Banikoara.
bj.why: The victory concludes a youth competition aimed at the development of young players in the region.

bj.headline: Djougou hosts 25th national primary school championships
bj.body: The final phase of the 25th National Primary School Championships began on Monday, Aug. 17, in Djougou. The four-day event is organized by the Union des Associations Sportives et Culturelles de l'Enseignement Primaire.
bj.why: The event brings together young athletes from all departments of Benin to compete in sports and cultural activities.

bw.headline: MMG finds 1.4 million tonnes of copper at Khoemacau mine
bw.body: MMG Ltd discovered a new copper-silver deposit containing an estimated 1.4 million tonnes of copper and 90 million ounces of silver. The Kgwebe deposit is located approximately six kilometres from the existing Zone 5 mine.
bw.why: The discovery increases the long-term mineral resources and growth prospects for the Khoemacau operation.

bw.headline: Botswana inflation falls to 9.4% in July
bw.body: Annual inflation decreased to 9.4% in July from 10.7% in June. Statistics Botswana attributed the 1.3 percentage-point decline to a 6.5% drop in the transport index.
bw.why: Lower fuel prices have reduced transport costs for consumers and businesses.

bw.headline: African Development Bank values Botswana natural capital at $116 billion
bw.body: The African Development Bank estimated Botswana's natural capital, including wildlife and water, at $116 billion as of 2020. The figure represents the value of assets over time rather than available public spending.
bw.why: The government is seeking these natural assets as alternative sources of growth and financing to reduce dependence on diamonds.

bw.headline: Botswana retains P1,500 daily per diem for public servants
bw.body: The government maintained a P1,500 daily local per diem for public servants, according to the Hospitality and Tourism Association of Botswana. Starting Sept. 1, 2026, workers must provide receipts for up to P900 of the accommodation component.
bw.why: The policy is expected to increase demand for the domestic hospitality industry.

bw.headline: Botswana working-age population to reach 67.6% by 2038
bw.body: The population of people aged 15 to 64 is projected to rise to 67.6% by 2038. The Sunday Standard reports the trend creates a potential economic dividend.
bw.why: The government must generate more jobs and raise productivity to prevent the swelling population from becoming an economic burden.

bf.headline: Police intercept 7 minors headed for gold mining sites
bf.body: The Regional Brigade for the Protection of Children intercepted seven minors on Tuesday, Aug. 18, in Koudougou. The eldest of the group was 12 years old. The children were reportedly traveling to artisanal gold mining sites.
bf.why: The operation prevents children under the legal age from working in hazardous mining conditions.

bf.headline: AEEMB donates 1,000 kg of rice to patriotic immersion recruits
bf.body: The Association of Muslim Students of Burkina (AEEMB) donated 40 bags of rice, each weighing 25 kg, on Tuesday. The donation was delivered to recruits of the mandatory patriotic immersion at the VÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©nÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©grÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© municipal high school in Ouagadougou.
bf.why: The donation provides food supplies for students participating in the mandatory national service program.

bf.headline: UEMOA reports solid 2026 growth amid inflation risks
bf.body: The West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA) maintains strong economic momentum in 2026. Growth is driven by the construction, financial services, and trade sectors. Lefaso.net reports that insecurity and distribution difficulties in certain zones may increase price pressures.
bf.why: Distribution failures in insecure areas could raise the cost of essential goods for residents in those regions.

bi.headline: Burundi allocates 11 billion for university student meals
bi.body: The Burundian government plans to spend 11 billion to restart catering services for approximately 4,000 students at the University of Burundi. The program is scheduled to begin in September 2026, following an eight-year hiatus. SOS MÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©dias Burundi reported the funding details on August 19.
bi.why: Approximately 4,000 students will regain access to campus dining services after eight years without them.

bi.headline: Beer prices in Gitega double amid supply speculation
bi.body: Primus and Amstel beers are selling for double their official prices in Gitega. Iwacu reports the price spike follows revelations that Brarudi is exporting products to the DRC to compensate for a lack of foreign currency.
bi.why: Consumers in Gitega must pay twice the official rate to purchase beer due to redirected exports.

bi.headline: Gitega installs first operational medical scanner outside capital
bi.body: A medical scanner is now operational in Gitega. According to Yaga Burundi, it is the first scanner functioning outside of Bujumbura in 2026.
bi.why: Patients in Gitega can now access diagnostic scanning without traveling to Bujumbura.

bi.headline: Burundi opens judicial proceedings over illegal arms trafficking
bi.body: The General Prosecutor's Office announced the opening of a judicial procedure against a group of people. SOS MÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©dias Burundi reports the individuals are accused of involvement in illegal arms trafficking.
bi.why: The legal proceedings target individuals accused of smuggling weapons into the country.

bi.headline: Burundi beats Germany in Beach Pro Tour opener
bi.body: The Burundi men's team defeated Germany in the opening match of the Volleyball World Beach Pro Tour Bujumbura Futures 2026. The event is running from August 19 to 23 on the shores of Lake Tanganyika, according to Iwacu.
bi.why: The victory marks a successful start for the host nation in an international beach volleyball competition.

cm.body: President Paul Biya and his wife Chantal Biya landed at YaoundÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© Nsimalen International Airport on Aug. 20. The visit was the president's longest private stay in Europe, according to the Journal du Cameroun.
cm.why: The return ends a prolonged absence of the head of state from the capital.

cm.headline: Douala BRT project faces 104.6 billion CFA franc funding gap
cm.body: The Douala Urban Mobility Project requires an additional 104.6 billion CFA francs to maintain its current scope. As of July 17, 2026, the total cost to complete the project rose to 365.4 billion CFA francs from an initial budget of 260.8 billion CFA francs, according to Business in Cameroon.
cm.why: The shortfall may lead to a downsizing of the Bus Rapid Transit system and the removal of 66 kilometers of planned feeder roads.

cm.headline: Cameroon signs Bolongo offshore block deal with Octavia Energy
cm.body: Octavia Energy Corporation committed to an exploration program of up to $41 million under a production sharing contract signed Aug. 14. The agreement covers a 381.56-square-kilometre block, according to Business in Cameroon.
cm.why: The contract moves the offshore block into the exploration phase to determine potential hydrocarbon production.

cm.headline: Cameroon reports 45.5% BTS and 54.79% HND pass rates
cm.body: The Ministry of Higher Education published official 2026 results on Aug. 19, showing a 45.50% success rate for the BTS and 54.79% for the HND. These figures contradict earlier reports of a 14% pass rate, according to the Journal du Cameroun.
cm.why: The official data corrects previously circulated erroneous information regarding student graduation rates.

cm.headline: IsDB discusses 2027-2029 framework for Cameroon

cm.why: The meeting aims to establish a three-year partnership framework to manage the bank's financial packages and projects.

cf.headline: CAR government reports 49 dead in Zamboye mine collapse
cf.body: A total of 49 people died following earth collapses on Tuesday at the "Moscou-RCA" mining site in Zamboye. Minister of Mines and Geology Rufin Benam-Beltoungou provided the figure after visiting the site in Nana-MambÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©rÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©.

cf.headline: CAR Communications Minister arrives in Beijing for media forum
cf.body: Minister of State for Communication and Media Evariste Ngamana arrived in Beijing on August 18. He is attending the 7th China-Africa Media Forum.
cf.why: The visit is intended to strengthen diplomatic and media cooperation between the Central African Republic and China.

km.headline: Moroni authorities open investigation into abduction of 6-year-old girl
km.body: A 6-year-old girl is in grave condition after being abducted and raped on Aug. 16. Comores Infos reports the child disappeared while traveling to her Quranic school.
km.why: The incident has prompted a police investigation into the abduction and assault.

cg.headline: Congo sets $90 per barrel threshold for oil contracts
cg.body: The Council of Ministers approved texts to adapt the oil sector's contractual framework, including a single threshold of $90 per barrel. The measures include amendments for permits Nanga II Bis, Nanga IV, Nangua V, and Marine XXIX. The government also launched a redevelopment project for the Banga Kayo permit.
cg.why: The adjustment to the technical mechanism aims to support investments and increase oil production.

cg.headline: Congo maintains cement prices for 50kg bags
cg.body: Cement prices remain unchanged at 4,900 FCFA in Brazzaville, 4,700 FCFA in Pointe-Noire, and 5,500 FCFA in Ouesso for a 50kg bag. Producers Dangote, Sonocc, and Forspak agreed to maintain 2024 rates following a meeting with the Minister of Commerce on Aug. 19. The decision follows requests from producers for a price increase.
cg.why: The price freeze prevents immediate cost increases for construction materials for consumers in the three cities.

ci.why: The paved road improves transport and connectivity for residents of the Cavally region in western Ivory Coast.

ci.headline: Mining company installs hydraulic pump in Tiorotieri
ci.body: A mining company delivered an improved village hydraulic pump (HVA) to the people of Tiorotieri on Aug. 19. The Agence Ivoirienne de Presse reported the installation as part of the company's local development program.
ci.why: The new infrastructure provides the population of the Katogo sub-prefecture with improved access to water.

ci.why: The program provides financial or material incentives for students in the Songon district to maintain high academic performance.

eg.headline: Egypt secures $2 billion aluminum project in Suez Canal Zone
eg.body: Egypt has reached an agreement for a $2 billion investment in a high-tech aluminum project. Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs Hussein Issa finalized the deal with executives from a Chinese industrial firm.
eg.why: The investment establishes a global manufacturing engine for aluminum production within the Suez Canal Zone.

eg.headline: Egypt launches $658m phosphoric acid complex in New Valley
eg.body: Officials began construction Wednesday on a $658 million industrial complex at the Abu Tartour plateau. The facility is designed to produce 250,000 tonnes of commercial phosphoric acid annually.
eg.why: The plant will increase mining exports of fertilizer components via the Red Sea port.

The Egyptian Commercial Service said the deals cover copper, aluminium, sugar cane, oranges, leather, textile yarn and flax.
eg.why: The agreements diversify the types of Egyptian goods sold in the Chinese market.

eg.headline: Microbus rollover in Monufia kills 2, injures 17
eg.body: A passenger microbus overturned along the Kafr Dawood road near the village of Al-Baregat. The accident left two people dead and 17 others injured.
eg.why: The crash disrupted transit for passengers traveling near Al-Baregat in the Monufia Governorate.

eg.headline: Al-Sisi backs Libyan elections in talks with Khalifa Haftar
eg.body: President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi reiterated support for Libya's territorial unity and the holding of presidential and parliamentary elections. The statements were made during a Wednesday meeting with Libyan National Army commander Khalifa Haftar.
eg.why: The diplomatic support targets the unification of Libya's institutions.

gq.headline: Health Minister leaves 65,000 patients without antiretrovirals
gq.body: Approximately 65,000 patients in Bata are without antiretroviral medications. Diario Rombe reports that Health Minister DÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¡maso Mitoha OndoÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¢ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¡Ã‚Â¬ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Å¾Ã‚Â¢o Ayekaba has used media outlets to blame patients for abandoning treatment.
gq.why: The shortage of medication prevents thousands of HIV patients from maintaining viral suppression, increasing the risk of death.

gq.headline: Secret gold contract involves $30 million bank guarantee
gq.body: A secret contract involving 1,000 tons of gold and a $30 million bank guarantee was allegedly managed by a relative of Constancia Mangue. Diario Rombe reports the circuit operated outside of state controls and included facilities to purify raw gold.
gq.why: The use of an unofficial circuit for gold trade bypasses state regulatory controls and tax collection.

gq.headline: Scientific Committee validates V Population and I Agricultural censuses
gq.body: The Scientific Committee has approved the strategic documents for the fifth population census and the first agricultural census. The review took place at the Ministry of Finance, Budgets and National Planning.
gq.why: The validated technical instruments will allow the government to collect updated statistical data on the country's population and farming sector.

gq.headline: Media Law proposes new information sciences internship institute
gq.body: A proposed Media Law includes the creation of an internship institute for Information Sciences. Government delegates told deputies the institute is intended to organize the training of journalists in Equatorial Guinea.
gq.why: The institute would change how journalism students and professionals receive formal training and certification.

er.headline: Eritrea opens National Conference on Eritrean Agricultural Studies
er.body: The National Conference on Eritrean Agricultural Studies 2026 opened Aug. 20 at the National Confederation of Eritrean Workers Hall in Asmara. The event focuses on advancing sustainable agri-food systems for national economic growth, according to the state news agency Shabait.
er.why: The conference brings together ministers, experts, and food processors to coordinate strategies for increasing national economic growth through food systems.

ke.headline: IEBC requires public officers to resign by Feb. 10
ke.body: Public officers seeking elective posts must resign by February 10. The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) stated that campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before the polls.
ke.why: Government employees must leave their current roles by the February deadline to legally run for office.

ke.headline: IEBC targets 28.5 million voters for 2027 election
ke.body: The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) is targeting a voter register of 28.5 million people. The commission is also doubling the number of countries where diaspora voting is available.
ke.why: The expanded register would add more than six million people to the voting rolls ahead of the general election.

ke.headline: NANIB seizes Sh3.3 million cannabis in Narok
ke.body: The National Anti-Narcotics Investigations Bureau (NANIB) seized cannabis valued at Sh3.3 million. Detectives arrested three suspects following intelligence on the storage and distribution of the narcotics.
ke.why: The operation removes Sh3.3 million worth of illegal narcotics from the Narok distribution network.

ke.headline: Kenya schools to open Aug. 24
ke.body: Schools will open for Term III on August 24. Education CS Julius Ogamba issued the date to refute social media reports of a postponement.
ke.why: Parents must prepare students to return to classrooms by the August 24 date.

ke.headline: Ministry proposes split of tourism levy collection and management
ke.body: The Ministry is proposing the separation of tourism levy collection from funds management. Tourism PS Julius Bitok said the move mirrors the roles of the KRA and the CBK.
ke.why: The change would shift how tourism funds are collected and managed by creating two specialized roles.

za.headline: Eastern Cape Education Department admits withholding billions from schools
za.body: The Eastern Cape Education Department unlawfully withheld billions from schools, affecting 1.58 million no-fee pupils over three years. The admission was reported by Daily Maverick and GroundUp.
za.why: Parents already on grants must now supply their own toilet paper, cleaning products and copying paper for classrooms.

za.headline: Former PIC chair alleges board lacked legal opinion on Lanseria deal
za.body: Former Public Investment Corporation board chairperson David Masondo alleged CEO Patrick Dlamini failed to provide the board with a key legal opinion regarding the Lanseria Airport transaction. The claim was reported by Mail & Guardian.
za.why: The missing information raises questions about whether directors had the data required to exercise oversight during a governance crisis.

za.headline: MP Fadiel Adams accuses police officials of abusing power
za.body: National Coloured Congress MP Fadiel Adams told the Madlanga Commission that KZN police commissioner Lieutenant-General Nhlanhla Mkhwanazi and Crime Intelligence head Dumisani Khumalo colluded and abused power. The testimony was reported by Mail & Guardian.
za.why: Adams is calling for an investigation into Mkhwanazi following allegations involving Crime Intelligence.

za.headline: Hundreds of Johannesburg residents remain in Wembley Stadium shelter
za.body: Hundreds of residents continue to live in squalid conditions at Wembley Stadium years after being promised temporary shelter. The situation was reported by Daily Maverick and GroundUp.
za.why: Residents remain trapped among rubbish and rats with no clear path to permanent housing.

ng.headline: NESG forecasts Nigeria oil output to exceed 1.7mbpd
ng.body: Nigeria's crude oil production is expected to top 1.7 million barrels per day in the second half of 2026. The Nigerian Economic Summit Group reports that higher crude oil prices could improve the country's fiscal outlook.
ng.why: Increased production and pricing would provide the federal government with more revenue to fund public spending.

ng.headline: Ebola fatality rate climbs above 46%
ng.body: The fatality rate for the Ebola outbreak in Africa has risen above 46%. Nairametrics reports that health systems in affected areas are under increasing pressure as the outbreak nears pandemic-emergency status.
ng.why: The rising death rate and system strain increase the risk of the disease spreading beyond current containment zones.

ng.headline: Edo State inaugurates solar grid in Gbelebu
ng.body: Governor Monday Okpebholo has inaugurated a mini solar power grid in Gbelebu. The governor used the event to call for partnerships from investors and businesses operating in the state.
ng.why: The new grid provides a decentralized power source for residents and businesses in the Gbelebu area.

ng.headline: Atiku vows to restore petrol subsidy if elected in 2027
ng.body: ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore the petrol subsidy if elected president in 2027. He stated that individuals who diverted public funds from the previous scheme should be held accountable.
ng.why: Restoring the subsidy would lower the pump price of fuel for Nigerian motorists and transport operators.

ng.headline: AFRAA admits Enugu Air as member
ng.body: The African Airlines Association (AFRAA) has admitted Enugu Air into its membership. The move extends the association's base within Nigeria's domestic aviation sector.
ng.why: Membership in the association provides Enugu Air with a network for operational growth and industry collaboration.

et.headline: Ethiopia joins African Circular Economy Facility implementation
et.body: Ethiopia has entered the active implementation phase of the African Circular Economy Facility (ACEF). The African Development Bank (AfDB) manages the multi-donor trust fund.
et.why: The initiative aims to transform waste into economic value to foster green industrial development.

gh.headline: Mental Health Authority moves to close Kumasi centre housing 2,000 patients
gh.body: The Mental Health Authority has begun steps to shut down an illegal spiritual healing centre in Kumasi. The facility reportedly houses more than 2,000 people with mental health conditions.
gh.why: The closure removes 2,000 patients from an unlicensed spiritual facility to ensure they receive regulated mental health care.

gh.headline: Ablekuma North MP provides school items for 500 students
gh.body: Member of Parliament Ewurabena Aubynn provided essential educational items to 500 Basic Education Certificate Examination graduates. The students are preparing to enter senior high schools across the country.
gh.why: The provision of these materials allows 500 freshmen from the constituency to begin their senior high school education.

cd.headline: DR Congo launches emergency Ebola measures along Congo River
cd.body: The government launched an emergency system on Thursday between Kisangani and Kinshasa. An official communique stated the measures aim to prevent the spread of the Bundibugyo virus along the country's primary waterway.
cd.why: The measures restrict or monitor movement on the main fluvial route to stop the virus from reaching Kinshasa.

cd.headline: CAVB moves 2026 Men's African Volleyball Championship to Tunis
cd.body: The African Volleyball Confederation officialized the withdrawal of the Democratic Republic of Congo as host on Thursday. The event was originally scheduled for Kinshasa.
cd.why: The relocation removes the tournament from Kinshasa due to Ebola concerns.

cd.headline: AFC-M23 bans Kinshasa news broadcasts in South Kivu
cd.body: De facto governor Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi Shombo prohibited the broadcast of political programs in rebel-controlled zones. The ban includes the relay of information originating from Kinshasa.
cd.why: Residents in AFC-M23 controlled areas are now blocked from accessing official government information and political broadcasts.

cd.headline: Civil society denounces bank salary deductions in Kwilu
cd.body: Civil society president Brunel Ndombe reported that a local commercial bank is making deductions from the salaries of state officials and teachers. The group is demanding an explanation regarding the legality of the withholdings.
cd.why: Public employees in Kwilu are receiving lower take-home pay due to these unauthorized bank withdrawals.

tz.headline: Hydropower generates 63.85% of Tanzania's national grid electricity
tz.body: Hydropower provided 63.85% of electricity from the National Grid in 2025, according to the Tanzania Economic Survey 2025. Natural gas accounted for 31.48% of generation. Hydropower had an installed capacity of 2,718.27 MW compared to 1,140.72 MW for natural gas.
tz.why: The energy mix supports a national target to reach 3,000 kWh per capita by 2050.

tz.headline: Tanzania shutters Mwanahalisi news outlet for six months
tz.body: The state has suspended the Kiswahili investigative weekly Mwanahalisi for six months. The closure follows a report by the outlet regarding the Vice President, according to The Chanzo.
tz.why: The suspension restricts the availability of investigative reporting in the Kiswahili language.

tz.headline: Tanzania gives cement makers eight days to cut prices
tz.body: The government has issued an eight-day ultimatum to cement manufacturers to reduce prices and improve supplies. The order was reported by The Citizen.
tz.why: Lower prices would reduce construction costs for builders and homeowners.

tz.headline: Coop Bank opens seventh branch to target rural growth
tz.body: Coop Bank has expanded its national footprint to seven branches. The lender is accelerating growth in rural areas, according to The Citizen.
tz.why: The expansion increases access to banking services for residents in rural regions.

tz.headline: NECTA head elected president of AEAA for 2026/2027 term
tz.body: Prof. Said Mohamed, Executive Secretary of the National Examinations Council of Tanzania, was elected president of the Association for Educational Assessment in Africa. He pledged to increase transparency and accountability within the organization.
tz.why: The appointment places a Tanzanian official in charge of coordinating educational assessment challenges across Africa.

ma.headline: Morocco to host home matches for nine African national teams
ma.body: Morocco will host home fixtures for nine African teams during the opening window of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. The teams include Niger, Lesotho, Central African Republic, Liberia, Benin, Togo, Guinea, Madagascar and Somalia. The move follows a determination that these nations' domestic stadiums do not meet Confederation of African Football standards.
ma.why: The arrangement allows these nine teams to compete in qualifiers despite lacking approved domestic infrastructure.

ma.headline: Algeria returns 49 migration candidates to Morocco
ma.body: Algerian authorities returned 49 Moroccan migration candidates via the Oujda-Maghnia border crossing on Wednesday. ma.why: The transfer returns these 49 individuals to Moroccan jurisdiction after their attempt to migrate.

ma.headline: Morocco investigates money laundering at three casinos
ma.body: The National Financial Intelligence Authority is investigating suspected money laundering through poker games at three casinos in Marrakech and Agadir. Sources told Hespress that gamblers are suspected of presenting funds of unknown origin as winnings to deposit into bank accounts.
ma.why: Investigators are comparing declared winnings with game records to identify the origin of the funds.

ma.why: The loss of the Lithuanian plant's capacity tightens global supplies for European agricultural buyers.

ma.headline: Gharb municipalities report no mosquito surge after floods
ma.body: Municipal authorities in the Gharb region reported no unusual increase in mosquitoes during the first summer following recent floods. Officials attributed the result to early drainage and pest-control operations.
ma.why: The measures prevented stagnant flood waters from becoming breeding grounds for insects.

ug.headline: Uganda trade deficit widens to $598 million in June
ug.body: Uganda's merchandise trade deficit reached approximately $598 million in June. The Nile Post reports imports grew three times faster than exports, while coffee earnings decreased by more than one-third.
ug.why: The drop in coffee earnings and surge in imports reduces the amount of foreign currency available to the state.

ug.headline: Kabalagala house attack kills two children
ug.body: Two children were killed and three people, including their mother, were injured in an early-morning attack in Kabalagala. Police are investigating the incident, which also involved the burning of a vehicle.
ug.why: The attack resulted in the deaths of two minors and the destruction of private property.

ug.headline: Court convicts two school directors for pupil murder
ug.body: The High court in Soroti convicted Jozan Nursery and Primary School directors Suzan Vivian Ariokot and Joseph Okedi, and police officer John Bosco Obotol, for the murder of six-year-old Joan Faith Apio. The pupil was found dead in a school latrine on February 5, 2025.
ug.why: The ruling establishes legal accountability for school administrators regarding the death of a student on campus.

ug.headline: Movit Africa provides tuk-tuks to three Masaka traders
ug.body: Movit Africa gave tuk-tuks to three cosmetics traders in Masaka and Kyotera. The company stated the vehicles are intended to help traders move more stock and reduce transport costs.
ug.why: The new vehicles allow these specific traders to reach more customers and lower their operational overhead.

ug.headline: State witness claims Besigye plotted Cafe Javas bombing
ug.body: Investigator Andrew Wilson told the High court he used a hidden camera to record meetings where Dr. Kizza Besigye discussed acquiring weapons to overthrow the government. Wilson testified that these plans included bombing Cafe Javas.
ug.why: The testimony provides the court with alleged evidence of a plot to use explosives against a commercial target.

zw.headline: RBZ injects ZiG600 million into economy
zw.body: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe injected approximately ZiG600 million into circulation during the first half of 2026. The central bank stated the move aims to deepen the use of the local currency.
zw.why: The injection is intended to ease cash-related challenges for users of the local currency.

zw.headline: RBZ maintains 30% export surrender requirement
zw.body: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe rejected calls from exporters to reduce the 30% export surrender threshold. The central bank stated in its mid-term monetary policy statement that the policy is critical for price and exchange rate stability.
zw.why: Exporters must continue to surrender nearly one-third of their foreign currency earnings to the central bank.

zw.headline: Court grants USD1,000 bail to President's daughter-in-law
zw.body: Kelsea Tadiwa Tafirenyika and co-accused Isaac Arab Jessub were granted USD1,000 bail by the High Court. Justice Pisirayi Kwenda set aside a previous magistrate's decision from August 13 that had denied bail in a drug dealing case.
zw.why: The ruling allows the two accused individuals to leave custody pending their trial.

zw.headline: State owes contractors ZiG250 billion
zw.body: The Auditor-General estimates outstanding state payments to contractors at ZiG250 billion. Affected firms stated this week they are exploring private consultants to recover the funds due to cash-flow problems.
zw.why: Deepening cash-flow shortages are pushing the affected firms to the brink of failure.

zw.headline: Zimbabwe introduces tracking system after hospital drug thefts
zw.body: The government launched a medicine tracking system to stop the theft of drugs from public hospitals. Deputy Health Minister Sleiman Kwidini said the system targets the alleged resale of stolen medicines through private pharmacies.
zw.why: The system aims to ensure public hospital medicines reach patients rather than being diverted to private sellers.

cv.headline: Cape Verde opens 55,719 new payment accounts in 2025
cv.body: The country added 55,719 new payment accounts in 2025, bringing the total for resident individuals to 439,973. According to the document, 85.6% of the resident population now holds at least one bank account. The number of bank branches fell by two to 127 during the year.
cv.why: The decline in physical branches reflects a shift toward the use of banking agents to provide financial services.

cv.headline: Cape Verde government meets mayors to align budget priorities
cv.body: Government head Francisco Carvalho held meetings with mayors from Santiago island to align local priorities with the State Budget. Carvalho stated the administration is conducting a round of direct dialogue with mayors to hear the priorities of each territory. He noted that all municipalities will be treated equally.
cv.why: These consultations determine how state funds are allocated to specific local infrastructure and service projects.

td.headline: N'Djamena police clear illegal site at Milezi forest
td.body: Municipal police and national security forces cleared an illegally occupied public space in the 1st arrondissement on Aug. 20. The operation took place at the Milezi forest. The site is designated for future development.
td.why: The clearance removes irregular occupants to allow the city to proceed with planned construction on the site.

td.body: Comedian Cache-Cache Le Haut Niveau represented Chad at the third 'Marionnettes en Marche' festival in YaoundÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© from July 30 to Aug. 2. Following the event, he called for a relaunch of puppet theater in Chad.
td.why: The push aims to restore a traditional art form that the performer claims is currently declining.

td.headline: Chad and Libya discuss economic cooperation in Tripoli
td.body: Chadian Foreign Minister Dr. Abdoulaye Sabre Fadoul met with the Libyan Finance Minister in Tripoli. The officials discussed ways to increase bilateral economic cooperation.
td.why: The talks aim to increase trade and financial ties between the two neighboring countries.

td.headline: Alwihda Info coordinator returns to N'Djamena from Egypt
td.body: Malick Mahamat Tidjani returned to N'Djamena on Aug. 20. He had been detained by police in Egypt for several days.
td.why: The return ends the detention of the media coordinator and resolves the situation regarding his status in Egypt.

dj.headline: Djibouti economy grows 6.7% in 2025
dj.body: Djibouti's economy grew by 6.7% in 2025, down from 6.8% in 2024. The African Development Bank reported the growth was driven by telecommunications, energy, trade, construction, and port and logistics activities.
dj.why: The continued expansion of port and logistics activities supports the country's primary revenue streams from maritime trade.

sz.headline: Eswatini to pave 250km of roads for E1.6 billion
sz.body: Approximately 250 kilometres of untarred roads across four regions will be paved using Probase tarring at a cost of E1.6 billion. The project was detailed during a meeting between the King, Probase, and Exim Bank.
sz.why: The project replaces untarred surfaces with paved roads across all four of the country's regions.

sz.headline: King gives US$1,000 to Eswatini students in Malaysia
sz.body: The King provided a contribution of US$1,000, or approximately E16,000, to each Eswatini student studying in Malaysia. Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Pholile Shakantu announced the gift during a courtesy call.
sz.why: The funds provide direct financial support for the welfare of students studying abroad.

sz.headline: MPs pass motion to establish health fund levies
sz.body: Members of Parliament passed a motion to establish a fund for collecting levies to fight serious diseases. The motion was moved by Lobamba Lomdzala MP Marwick Khumalo and seconded by Somntongo MP Sandile Nxumalo.
sz.why: The fund creates a new mechanism to collect and channel money specifically toward treating serious diseases.

sz.headline: Eswatini athletes eligible for E8.9m Comrades prize purse
sz.body: An E8.9 million prize purse is available for Eswatini elite athletes in the 100th Comrades Marathon. The centenary edition of the ultramarathon is scheduled for June 13, 2027.
sz.why: The prize money provides a financial incentive for elite athletes competing in the centenary event.

sz.headline: SBS Bank schedules first AGM after commercial conversion
sz.body: SBS Bank Eswatini will hold its first annual general meeting on September 4, 2026, at the Royal Villas Hotel. The meeting follows the institution's transition from the Swaziland Building Society into a commercial bank.
sz.why: The meeting marks the first formal shareholder gathering since the entity changed its legal status to a commercial banking institution.

ga.headline: Gabon repatriates 28 citizens from South Africa
ga.body: Twenty-eight Gabonese citizens returned to Libreville on Wednesday via a Fly Gabon flight. The repatriation follows xenophobic tensions in South Africa, according to Gabon Actu.
ga.why: The move provides immediate safety for citizens, including those who were in South Africa under irregular status.

ga.headline: Agasa immobilizes 10 bread transport vehicles
ga.body: The Gabonese Food Safety Agency (Agasa) has grounded approximately 10 vehicles in the Estuaire region since Aug. 14. The agency is conducting a national compliance campaign for vehicles transporting bread and bakery products.
ga.why: Bakery distributors using non-compliant vehicles face operational shutdowns until they meet safety standards.

ga.headline: Authorities arrest 4 people for trafficking baby chimpanzee
ga.body: Four individuals were detained in Libreville on Aug. 12 while attempting to illegally sell a nine-month-old baby chimpanzee. The animal was transferred to the LÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©kÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©di park, according to Gabon Review.
ga.why: The seizure removes a protected species from the illegal wildlife trade and returns it to a managed sanctuary.

ga.why: The appointment establishes a formal social dialogue structure for municipal employees to voice grievances to city leadership.

ga.headline: CF Mounana signs midfielder Franck Engonga
ga.body: CF Mounana announced the return of Gabonese midfielder Franck Engonga. The signing is part of the club's recruitment for the 2026-2027 season.
ga.why: The addition of Engonga changes the squad composition for the club's upcoming National-Foot 1 campaign.

gm.headline: Gambia to play Somalia at Independence Stadium next month
gm.body: The national team will play its first Afcon 2027 qualifier against Somalia at the Independence Stadium. Coach Jonathon McKinstry announced the venue for the match scheduled for next month.
gm.why: This marks the first time since McKinstry took over as coach in May 2024 that the team will play a home match.

gm.headline: IGP meets security chiefs on election coordination
gm.body: The Inspector General of Police hosted service chiefs to coordinate security preparations for the upcoming electoral process. The meeting focused on information sharing and public safety.
gm.why: The engagement aims to establish a professional security approach to maintain order throughout the electoral period.

gm.headline: Minister cites mathematics teacher shortage as major challenge
gm.body: Dr. Drammeh stated that a shortage of mathematics teachers is a significant factor in poor student performance. She attributed the gap to low enrollment in mathematics at the tertiary level.
gm.why: The lack of staff means some schools currently operate without a mathematics teacher.

gm.headline: UDP claims state bias in conference center access
gm.body: UDP Deputy Administrative Secretary Dr. Lamin Manneh alleged the party was repeatedly denied use of the Sir Dawda Kairaba Jawara International Conference Centre. The party was denied access for its 30th anniversary and a strategic retreat despite offering to pay commercial fees.
gm.why: The restriction prevents the political party from using state-owned facilities for major organizational events.

gn.headline: CSM revokes Supreme Court prosecutor Algassimou Diallo
gn.body: The Superior Council of the Magistracy revoked Algassimou Diallo, the general prosecutor at the Supreme Court, on Aug. 20. The disciplinary action followed a referral by Justice Minister Ibrahima Sory 2 Tounkara regarding failures to meet statutory obligations.
gn.why: The decision removes the general prosecutor from his post and may lead to his permanent disbarment.

gn.headline: Rio Tinto SimFer delivers 5 schools in Beyla
gn.body: The SimFer joint venture delivered five new schools to educational authorities in Beyla. According to the company, the facilities provide education access for more than 1,700 students from communities near the Simandou Project.
gn.why: The new infrastructure increases classroom capacity for 1,700 children in the riverine communities of the mining project.

gn.headline: BCRG warns against unauthorized crypto-asset platforms
gn.body: The Central Bank of the Republic of Guinea (BCRG) issued a warning against the use of illegal trading and crypto-asset investment platforms. The bank stated in an official communique that it has not issued any legal authorizations for these financial services.
gn.why: The alert warns the public that investments in these unauthorized online platforms lack legal protection from the central bank.

gn.headline: Fire in Simambossya kills 2 children
gn.body: Two children died in a house fire in the Cantine sector of the Simambossya neighborhood on Aug. 19. The blaze occurred around 1 p.m. in a family residence in the Lambanyi urban commune.
gn.why: The incident resulted in the deaths of two children and affected residents of the Simambossya neighborhood.

gn.headline: Guinea basketball team begins World Cup qualifiers in Tunisia
gn.body: The national basketball team will compete in the second phase of the 2027 FIBA World Cup qualifiers from Aug. 27 to 30. The games will take place in RadÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¨s, Tunisia, following the team's successful first round.
gn.why: The matches determine if the national team secures a place among the elite African teams for the 2027 World Cup.

gw.headline: CNE bars political parties from Aug. 30 referendum campaign
gw.body: Political parties are excluded from participating in the campaign for the Aug. 30 referendum. National Election Commission President Carmem Isaura Tavares Batista Lobo cited the Referendum Law as the basis for the restriction.
gw.why: The ruling prevents organized political parties from officially campaigning for or against the proposed constitutional changes.

lr.headline: Liberia collects US$904.7 million in domestic revenue
lr.body: The Liberia Revenue Authority reported US$904.7 million in domestic revenue collection as of August 18. The figure brings the government closer to a US$1 billion mark. This allows the government to strengthen domestic resource mobilization.
lr.why: Increased domestic revenue reduces the government's reliance on external funding for public spending.

lr.headline: Unity Party backs security probe into Jewel Howard Taylor
lr.body: The governing Unity Party commended Joint Security for charges against former Vice President Jewel Howard Taylor. The charges relate to a multimillion-dollar cocaine probe. The party urged security agencies to remain professional despite public pressure.
lr.why: The party's support signals a commitment to pursuing high-level officials involved in narcotics trafficking.

lr.headline: Liberia signs new Satellite Communications Guidelines
lr.body: LTA Chairperson Massaquoi and Minister of Posts and Telecommunications Sekou M. Kromah signed new Satellite Communications Guidelines. The officials displayed the signed copy of the document on Tuesday.
lr.why: The new guidelines establish the regulatory framework for satellite service providers operating in the country.

lr.headline: AMEU and University of Sierra Leone renew partnership
lr.body: The African Methodist Episcopal University and the Institute of Public Administration and Management at the University of Sierra Leone renewed an academic cooperation agreement on Tuesday. The partnership focuses on joint research and faculty and student exchanges.
lr.why: Students and faculty at both institutions gain access to postgraduate opportunities and knowledge transfer across borders.

ly.headline: Spanish exports to Libya rise 114.6%
ly.body: Spanish exports to Libya increased by 114.6% and Libyan imports to Spain rose 66.8% during the first six months of the year. The Spanish Embassy in Libya provided the data.
ly.why: The growth increases the volume of trade goods moving between the two nations.

ly.headline: Libyan health center distributes 300 solar refrigerators
ly.body: The National Centre for Disease Control distributed more than 300 solar-powered refrigerators. The move follows reports of medical supplies perishing due to summer power cuts.
ly.why: The equipment prevents the loss of temperature-sensitive medical supplies during blackouts.

ly.headline: Libya sets new hard currency ceilings for companies
ly.body: The Ministry of Economy and Trade adopted a new mechanism to set ceilings on foreign currency for companies. The formula considers tax payments, employment, and economic activity.
ly.why: Companies must now meet specific employment and tax criteria to obtain hard currency.

ly.headline: Libyan prosecutor detains 9 over citizenship forgery
ly.body: The Public Prosecutor ordered the detention of a civil registry employee and eight beneficiaries in Al-Khums. The group is accused of forging documents to grant citizenship rights unlawfully.
ly.why: The arrests target the illegal acquisition of citizenship rights through forged civil status data.

ly.headline: Libya and Chad to resume direct flights
ly.body: Prime Minister Abdel Hamid Aldabaiba and the Chadian Minister of Foreign Affairs discussed the resumption of direct flights. The flights are scheduled to start tomorrow.
ly.why: The agreement restores direct air travel between the two countries.

mg.headline: SADC urges Madagascar to return to constitutional normality
mg.body: The Southern African Development Community issued recommendations on democratic functioning and human rights following its 46th Summit in Durban. The regional organization stated the support is contingent on inclusive governance and citizen participation.
mg.why: The requirements for accountability and human rights must be met for Madagascar to regain full constitutional normality.

mg.body: Colonel MichaÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â«l Randrianirina stated that ongoing political consultations are necessary to accelerate the electoral process. The president said the move is intended to assist the CENI in preparing for upcoming votes.
mg.why: The dialogue is intended to determine the timeline and preparation for the next national elections.

mg.headline: Antananarivo residents face water and power outages
mg.body: Water pressure drops and electricity cuts have returned to several districts of the capital over the last few days. JIRAMA announced that these disruptions are expected to continue into next week.
mg.why: Residents in the capital's affected sectors will lack consistent access to basic utilities for at least one more week.

mg.headline: Mpox vaccinations begin at Polytechnique Vontovorona
mg.body: Health officials have started administering Mpox vaccines to students at the Polytechnique Vontovorona campus. The campaign includes awareness efforts to encourage students to protect themselves from the epidemic.
mg.why: Students at the Vontovorona campus now have direct access to vaccinations to prevent the spread of Mpox.

mg.headline: French parliamentary delegation visits Madagascar
mg.body: Bruno Fuchs, chairman of the French National Assembly's foreign affairs commission, met with MichaÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â«l Randrianirina on August 19. The discussions focused on cooperation as Madagascar reconfigures its international relations.
mg.why: The visit allows the current authorities to maintain diplomatic ties with France during a period of international realignment.

mw.headline: Malawi loses $700 million in gold to smugglers
mw.body: Malawi loses an estimated $700 million worth of gold to smugglers annually. Mining Minister Thoko Tembo said the Malawi Mining Investment Company is establishing mining cooperatives and formal structures to address the trade.
mw.why: The government is implementing new measures to formalize the mining sector to recover lost revenue.

mw.headline: Youths account for 80% of population excluded from formal economy
mw.body: Approximately 80% of Malawi's population is excluded from or passively participating in economic activities. Stakeholders at a youth conference in Lilongwe attributed the trend to disjointed policies and a lack of opportunities.
mw.why: The lack of formal economic structures limits the ability of young entrepreneurs to innovate and create businesses.

mw.headline: Continental Holdings shares drop 44% from peak
mw.body: Continental Holdings plc share prices have fallen approximately 44% from a listing day peak of K350 per share. Investors have urged shareholders to remain patient despite the tumble.
mw.why: The price drop affects the current valuation of holdings for shareholders of the company.

mw.headline: President Mutharika awards Scorchers players K5 million each
mw.body: President Peter Mutharika has given K5 million to each player of the Scorchers. The payments follow the team's Wafcon campaign in Rabat, Morocco.
mw.why: The cash rewards provide direct financial compensation to the athletes for their international performance.

mw.headline: Mozambique-Malawi power project misses third deadline
mw.body: The Mozambique-Malawi Interconnection Project has missed its commissioning deadline for a third time. The project is intended to provide stabilized electricity via an energy purchase deal.
mw.why: The delay extends the period of frequent power outages currently affecting Malawians.

ml.headline: Child dies in Kita after suspected poisoning
ml.body: A 7-year-old boy died Tuesday after allegedly consuming a toxic substance from a bottle of milk. Studio Tamani and Bamada.net report the child died during evacuation to Bamako. Police are currently questioning an unidentified woman suspected of the act.
ml.why: The incident has led to a police investigation into the death of a minor in the SÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©goubougouni neighborhood.

ml.headline: San residents donate 1 million CFA to military
ml.body: Residents of San delivered more than 1 million francs CFA to camp officials on Tuesday. ml.why: The mobilization provides direct financial support to military personnel following a security breach at the local camp.

mr.headline: Mauritanian opposition rejects calls for third presidential term
mr.body: The democratic opposition coalition rejected calls for a third presidential term on Wednesday. The group stated that attempts to bypass constitutional term limits would threaten the peaceful transfer of power.
mr.why: The move signals potential political instability if the government attempts to modify constitutional restrictions on the presidency.

mr.headline: Mauritania begins recruitment for 390 ministry agents
mr.body: Testing began Tuesday at the Nouakchott university campus to recruit 390 agents for several ministries. The exams are part of a larger initiative to hire 3,000 state contract employees.
mr.why: The hiring process increases the size of the state workforce across multiple government departments.

mr.headline: Moroccan customs seize 54kg of gold from Mauritanian family
mr.body: Moroccan authorities seized 54 kilograms of gold from a Mauritanian couple and three minor children at Mohammed V International Airport in Casablanca. The family was referred to the judicial police for investigation.
mr.why: The seizure and subsequent police investigation restrict the movement and assets of the affected family members.

mr.headline: Vehicle fire destroys 34 million old ouguiyas in Arafat
mr.body: A vehicle transporting funds for several money transfer agencies caught fire in the Arafat moughata of Nouakchott-Sud. The owner of a transfer agency estimated the lost sum at 34 million old ouguiyas.
mr.why: The loss of funds affects the liquidity of the multiple money transfer agencies involved in the shipment.

mr.headline: Mauritanian gendarmerie dismantles drug network in Nouakchott
mr.body: The Mauritanian gendarmerie announced Tuesday that it arrested members of a network selling narcotics and psychotropic substances in Nouakchott. The operation was conducted by the 1st company of Nouakchott and mixed brigades.
mr.why: The arrests remove a distribution network of illegal substances from the capital city.

mu.headline: Supreme Court annuls release of inspector in Rs 75.9M drug case
mu.body: The Supreme Court overturned the release of Inspector Vicky Luckmun regarding the importation of Rs 75.9 million in synthetic drugs. The ruling was reported by Defi Media.
mu.why: The decision reinstates legal proceedings against a police official involved in a high-value narcotics trafficking case.

mu.headline: IT Unit clones phone of Veronique Leu-Govind
mu.body: The IT Unit cloned the telephone of Veronique Leu-Govind. The incident was reported by Defi Media and Ion News.
mu.why: The breach compromises the digital privacy and communications security of a public figure.

mu.headline: Mauritius water production falls 17.8% through July
mu.body: Global water production decreased by 17.8% compared to the previous year as of late July. Central Water Authority figures reported by Ion News indicate the Mare aux Vacoas reservoir has been hit harder by rainfall deficits than other reservoirs.
mu.why: Lower production levels reduce the available water supply for residents and businesses relying on the national grid.

mu.headline: Indian Oil to deliver first fuel shipment in late September
mu.body: A first cargo of fuel from Indian Oil is expected to arrive in Mauritius at the end of September. The delivery was reported by Defi Media.
mu.why: The arrival of this shipment changes the fuel supply source for the country's energy infrastructure.

mu.headline: MSM holds second mobilization rally in Sainte-Croix on Thursday
mu.body: The Mouvement socialiste militant (MSM) will hold a rally in constituency No. 4 on August 20 starting at 17:00. Ion News reports the event is part of a restructuring effort following the party's defeat in the November 2024 general elections.
mu.why: The party is attempting to rebuild its grassroots base to regain political influence in the Port-Louis Nord/Montagne-Longue area.

mz.headline: ExxonMobil awards $1.1 billion in Rovuma LNG equipment contracts
mz.body: ExxonMobil Mozambique awarded approximately $1.1 billion in pre-investment contracts for long-term critical equipment for Phase 1 of the Rovuma LNG Project in Cabo Delgado. The company issued the contracts on behalf of Area 4 partners.
mz.why: The investment secures the long-lead equipment necessary to advance the development of the natural gas project.

mz.headline: BCI first-half profit falls to 3.3 billion meticais
mz.body: Profit for Banco Comercial e de Investimentos fell to 3.3 billion meticais from 3.7 billion meticais in the first half of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. The bank reported a spike in reserves due to high credit risk from non-performing loans.
mz.why: Increased reserves for bad loans have reduced the bank's net earnings for the first six months of the year.

mz.headline: Mozambique collects $43.83 million from Rovuma gas in first half
mz.body: The Mozambican state collected $43.83 million from the production and export of liquefied natural gas from the Rovuma basin between January and June 2026. The figure is based on the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (PESOE) balance.
mz.why: These funds increase the total state revenue from the extractive industry to $296.65 million.

mz.headline: Over 9,000 Mozambicans find work abroad since January
mz.body: More than 9,000 citizens were placed in mining and farming sectors in South Africa since January. National Directorate of Migrant Labor Director Alice Brito reported that new recruitment is underway for Portugal and the United Arab Emirates.
mz.why: The program provides employment opportunities for Mozambican workers in foreign agricultural and mining industries.

mz.headline: Police commander and two foreigners detained for illegal mining
mz.body: The police commander of Chinde district, a Portuguese citizen, and a Chinese citizen were detained on Monday, Aug. 17. Agents from the Sofala Customs Court and the Mozambique Republic Police (PRM) arrested the three on suspicion of illegal tantalite exploitation.
mz.why: The arrests target the illegal extraction of minerals in the ZambÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©zia province.

na.headline: Namibia non-bank sector assets reach N$552.8 billion
na.body: Namibia's non-bank financial sector assets have grown to more than N$552.8 billion. Imanuel Hawanga, general manager of capital markets at NAMFISA, also estimated the broader capital market ecosystem at N$338.2 billion.
na.why: The growth in these assets increases the capacity of non-bank institutions to mobilize savings and finance economic activity.

na.headline: Namibian Cabinet approves oil and gas local content policy
na.body: The Cabinet has approved the National Upstream Petroleum Local Content Policy. Kornelia Shilunga, head of the Upstream Petroleum Unit in the office of the President, announced the approval on Wednesday.
na.why: The policy allows for increased Namibian participation in the country's emerging oil and gas industry.

na.headline: Walvis Bay gives car wash operators 14 days to vacate
na.body: The municipality has given car wash operators 14 days to vacate road reserves along Sam Nujoma Avenue and Independence Road. The municipality stated the businesses were operating without required approvals and permits.
na.why: The eviction threatens the livelihoods of workers and the viability of the affected businesses.

na.headline: Namibia introduces business employment permit
na.body: The ministry of home affairs, immigration, safety and security has introduced the Employment Permit to Conduct Business. The permit was created through an amendment to Regulation 17 of the Immigration Control Act, 1993.
na.why: The new permit simplifies the process for investors and businesspersons seeking to establish or conduct business in the country.

na.headline: Minors hospitalized after drinking vodka from truck accident
na.body: Several minors were taken to the Otavi Clinic for medical attention after consuming alcoholic drinks. The beverages were recovered from a truck accident that occurred Tuesday morning near Otavi.
na.why: The consumption of potentially dangerous beverages led to the hospitalization of children in the Otavi area.

ne.headline: Niamey court records 420 infractions
ne.body: The Niamey High Court (TGI) recorded 420 total infractions during its seventh prosecutor's meeting of 2026. The cases were reported on August 14 by the Procureur de la RÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©publique. The majority of the offenses were terrorist in nature.
ne.why: The high volume of terrorism-related cases increases the judicial workload for the Niamey court system.

ne.headline: Abdou Moumouni University expects 20,000 new students
ne.body: The University Abdou Moumouni Dioffo expects 20,000 new graduates for the 2026-2027 academic year. Recteur Professor Moussa BaragÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© stated the institution currently has more than 42,000 students, with women making up 31.4% of the 2025-2026 enrollment.
ne.why: The influx of 20,000 new students will increase demand for capacity across the university's 200 programs.

ne.headline: Diffa sees 27 candidates for excellence school exams
ne.body: Twenty-seven candidates sat for the entrance exams for the LycÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©es d'Excellence of Niamey and Tessaoua in Diffa. Governor General Mahamadou Ibrahim Bagadoma launched the written tests on August 20 at the Fanna Grema primary school.
ne.why: The results determine which students from the Diffa region will gain admission to specialized secondary schools in Niamey and Tessaoua.

rw.headline: Rwanda low birth weight rate rises to 8.8%
rw.body: The proportion of babies born weighing less than 2.5 kilograms reached 8.8% in 2025. The National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda reported the figure in the Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey (RDHS7).
rw.why: The increase in low birth weight affects neonatal health outcomes for newborns and their mothers.

rw.headline: Rwanda Primary Leaving Examination cohort grows by 50,000
rw.body: The 2025-2026 Primary Leaving Examination cohort increased by more than 50,000 candidates compared to the previous year. Results from the national examinations show an increase in successful students.
rw.why: The growth in candidate numbers requires the education system to accommodate more students in classrooms.

rw.headline: WFP delivers 5,000 metric tonnes of rice to three nations
rw.body: A 5,000-metric-tonne rice shipment from India was delivered to the Port of Dar es Salaam to support Rwanda, the DRC, and Burundi. The delivery was coordinated by DP World and the United Nations World Food Programme.
rw.why: The shipment provides food relief to communities in Rwanda facing acute food insecurity.

rw.headline: Rwanda seeks Japanese investment in mining
rw.body: The Rwanda Development Board met with a delegation of Japanese mining investors on Wednesday. The talks were led by RDB CEO Jean-Guy K. Afrika and Japanese Ambassador Nakajo Kazuya.
rw.why: The cooperation aims to increase capital investment and economic activity within Rwanda's mining sector.

rw.headline: Rwanda sends business delegation to Brazil
rw.body: A government and private-sector delegation is visiting Brazil from August 17 to 21, 2026. The mission is led by Ministry of Trade and Industry Permanent Secretary Chantal Tuyishimire and Ambassador Lawrence Manzi.
rw.why: The mission seeks to establish new partnerships in innovation, skills development, and trade between the two countries.

st.headline: Constitutional Court delays party list for Sept. 27 elections
st.body: The Constitutional Court of Sao Tome and Principe has not yet validated the list of political parties admitted to the Sept. 27 legislative elections. The court cited Article 41 of the electoral law, which grants judges 11 business days to decide on the admission of candidacies.
st.why: The delay leaves the final field of candidates for the legislative elections unconfirmed.

st.headline: AFAP opens tender for vehicle procurement
st.body: The AFAP has announced a tender for the acquisition of rolling stock in batches. The procurement is part of a social protection, resilience, and recovery project funded by the World Bank.
st.why: The acquisition of these vehicles will support the implementation of World Bank-funded social protection and recovery projects.

sn.headline: Senegal assembly creates commission to probe tax exemptions
sn.body: The National Assembly adopted a resolution Thursday to create a parliamentary inquiry commission into the management of tax exemptions and debt write-offs. The probe seeks to uncover several hundred billion FCFA in tax losses. The commission is led by the PASTEF party.
sn.why: The investigation targets the recovery of hundreds of billions of FCFA in lost revenue to potentially increase state funds.

sn.headline: Senegal expresses concern over U.S. sanctions on ICC official
sn.body: The Senegalese government expressed deep concern Thursday following U.S. sanctions announced Aug. 18 against International Criminal Court officials. The sanctions target Abdoulaye Seye, a member of the Court's Prosecutor's Office. Seye is Senegal's candidate for a judge position.
sn.why: The sanctions affect the professional standing and candidacy of a Senegalese national seeking a judicial seat at the ICC.

sn.headline: Senegal judicial pole opens probe into 37 billion FCFA rural power fund
sn.body: The PÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â´le judiciaire et financier opened a judicial investigation into the ASER scandal involving 37 billion francs CFA intended for rural electrification. The Collectif Sunu 37 Milliards cited procedural irregularities in a recent communique. The case involves the role of Seydou Kane regarding contract exemptions.
sn.why: The investigation tracks the potential misappropriation of 37 billion FCFA meant for rural electricity infrastructure.

sn.headline: Senegal assembly examines critical infrastructure security bill
sn.body: The National Assembly is reviewing a text on the protection of critical information infrastructures and the strengthening of digital security. The legislation introduces new measures to prevent cyber threats. The bill focuses on the security of strategic systems.
sn.why: The new measures change how the state prevents cyberattacks on essential national infrastructure.

sn.headline: Bamba Dieng fails Lazio medical over knee issues
sn.body: Senegalese forward Bamba Dieng will not join Lazio Rome after failing a medical examination Thursday. Reports from Gianluca Di Marzio indicate the exams revealed problems with the player's knee. Dieng is now pursuing a move to Red Star.
sn.why: The failed medical prevents the player from transferring to the Italian club and forces a change in his career destination.

sc.headline: Seychelles Postal Service begins Shein deliveries
sc.body: The Seychelles Postal Service has taken over the delivery of Shein parcels. Chief Executive for the Postal Sector Neddy Padayachy said the service began approximately one month ago.
sc.why: Customers ordering from the online retailer Shein now receive their packages through the national postal system.

sl.headline: Sungrow commissions RESPITE Solar-plus-Storage Project
sl.body: Sungrow has commissioned the RESPITE Solar-plus-Storage Project, the first national-scale power generation project connected to the grid in nearly a decade. The project was announced on August 19, 2026.
sl.why: The project increases the country's power generation capacity by integrating solar energy and storage into the national grid.

sl.headline: Sierra Leone launches Gender Accountability Framework
sl.body: The Ministry of Gender and Children's Affairs and UN Women launched the Gender Accountability Framework and the 2025 Annual Report on the GEWE Act 2022 on August 19, 2026.
sl.why: The framework establishes a reporting mechanism to track the implementation of the Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment Act.

sl.headline: President Bio warns Kush drug peddlers to stop sales
sl.body: President Julius Maada Bio called on sellers of the synthetic drug Kush to stop operations during a visit to the Harmful Drug Rehabilitation Facility in Hastings on October 30, 2025.
sl.why: The crackdown targets an illicit trade that the president says is wreaking havoc in the country.

sl.headline: Freetown to rebuild King Jimmy market
sl.body: The historic King Jimmy market in Freetown will be rebuilt into a modern indoor market, according to a report on August 20, 2026.
sl.why: The reconstruction replaces one of West Africa's oldest markets with a modern facility for traders.

so.headline: Al-Shabaab attacks in Mogadishu fall from 144 to 5
so.body: Recorded attacks by Al-Shabaab in Mogadishu declined from 144 to 5, according to a report by The Economist. The report indicates a shift in the city's security landscape.
so.why: The reduction in attacks improves safety for residents and businesses operating within the capital.

so.headline: Somali pirates demand $3 million for 10 Pakistani sailors
so.body: Pirates have demanded $3 million for the release of 10 Pakistani sailors held since April. A Pakistani minister reported the demand on Wednesday following the hijacking of an oil tanker.
so.why: The demand creates a financial liability for the sailors' employers or the Pakistani government to secure their release.

so.headline: Airstrike kills 4 suspected pirates off Somalia coast
so.body: An airstrike killed four suspected pirates on Tuesday off the coast of Garmaal in the Nugaal region. Puntland security officials said the strike followed the hijacking of a ship bound for Mogadishu.
so.why: The operation targets maritime hijackers to secure shipping lanes for commercial vessels.

so.headline: Somalia postpones Hirshabelle state elections
so.body: The Independent National Electoral and Boundaries Commission postponed parliamentary and local council elections in Hirshabelle state. The votes were scheduled for Thursday, Aug. 20.
so.why: The delay prevents the scheduled transition of power for local council and House of Representatives members.

so.headline: Former president blames government for 30 deaths in Baidoa
so.body: Former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed attributed the deaths of 30 people in Baidoa to the federal government of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Sharif stated the violence resulted from a change of power imposed by force in Southwest State in March.
so.why: The accusation heightens political tension between the former president and the current federal administration.

ss.headline: UN Commission warns sham elections could fuel South Sudan conflict
ss.body: The UN Commission on Human Rights in South Sudan warned Thursday that sham elections could lead to atrocities and conflict. The warning was issued in a new report. This risk threatens to expose citizens to renewed violence and insecurity during the planned voting process.
ss.why: Irregular elections could trigger a return to large-scale violence for civilians.

ss.headline: IRC delivers new health and education facilities in Aweil South
ss.body: The International Rescue Committee handed over two renovated primary schools and health facilities to authorities in Aweil South County. The project was funded by the World Bank. Local communities in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State now have increased access to essential medical and schooling services.
ss.why: Residents of Aweil South County gain direct access to renovated primary schools and clinics.

ss.headline: Governor Adil urges SPLA-IO and NAS to end violence
ss.body: Central Equatoria State Governor Emmanuel Adil Anthony called on the SPLA-IO and the National Salvation Front to stop fighting on Thursday. The appeal followed a 12-day period of activity. The governor stated that peace is necessary ahead of the country's planned general elections.
ss.why: Continued fighting between these armed groups threatens the stability required to hold general elections.

ss.headline: Humanitarian Minister assesses needs in Malakal
ss.body: Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management Albino Akol Atak led a delegation to Malakal in Upper Nile State on Thursday. The group was received by Governor James Koang Chol. The visit aims to identify the specific needs of affected communities in the region.
ss.why: The assessment determines how humanitarian aid will be distributed to affected populations in Upper Nile State.

sd.headline: Kordofan fighting displaces more than 200,000 people
sd.body: More than 200,000 people have been displaced across Sudan's Kordofan region. The International Organization for Migration reported the figures following an intensification of fighting.
sd.why: The mass movement of people disrupts local stability and increases the immediate need for emergency shelter and food aid in the region.

tg.headline: Togo reports 2,244.31 billion FCFA in domestic debt
tg.body: Togo's domestic debt totals 2,244.31 billion FCFA. The figure was discussed during a 'Deep Dive' meeting in LomÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© on July 30, 2026, involving public and private actors. The session aimed to identify constraints hindering private sector growth.
tg.why: High levels of domestic debt create financial constraints that limit the ability of private businesses to expand and invest.

tg.headline: Togo regulator denies receiving accreditation for French journalists
