The two French journalists were recently arrested in the country. The regulator issued the statement via a formal communiquÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©.
tg.why: The lack of official accreditation provides a legal basis for the government to restrict or penalize foreign journalists operating in the country.

tg.headline: Togo grants provisional release to one French journalist
tg.body: One of two French journalists arrested on July 27 in Kara was granted provisional release on August 20, 2026. The individuals and their local fixer appeared before an instruction judge in LomÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©. The second journalist remains in custody pending a decision.
tg.why: The partial release alters the legal status of the detained foreign nationals and the diplomatic tension between LomÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â© and Paris.

tg.headline: Togo Senate opens second extraordinary session of 2026
tg.body: The Togolese Senate began its second extraordinary session of the year on August 17, 2026. The session was convened at the request of President Faure Essozimna GnassingbÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©. Meetings are being held at the Palais des CongrÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â¨s in LomÃƒÆ’Ã†â€™Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â©.
tg.why: The extraordinary session allows the government to fast-track specific legislative priorities outside the regular parliamentary calendar.

tn.headline: Tunisia records 1,101 protests in July
tn.body: Tunisia saw 1,101 protest movements in July 2026, the highest monthly total since July 2016. The Tunisian Social Observatory reported that more than 60% of these mobilizations were linked to social problems.
tn.why: The record level of unrest indicates increasing public dissatisfaction with social conditions.

tn.headline: Tunis medina schedules Mouled procession for Aug. 25
tn.body: A procession will start at 9:30 a.m. on Tuesday, Aug. 25, at the zaouia of Sidi Mahrez. The event will move through the Tunis medina toward the zaouia of Sidi Ben Arous.
tn.why: The event organizes the movement of crowds and religious participants through the city center.

tn.headline: Black Sea tensions pressure Tunisian wheat imports
tn.body: Tunisia remains dependent on imported wheat despite a strong domestic cereal campaign. Webdo reports that attacks on ships and ports in the Black Sea expose the country to supply disruptions.
tn.why: Instability in this global grain basin threatens the availability of a primary food staple for the population.

tn.headline: Bottled mineral water shortages persist in Tunisia
tn.body: A shortage of bottled mineral water continues across the country. Kapitalis reports the scarcity remains visible in numerous supermarkets and retail points.
tn.why: The ongoing shortage limits consumer access to drinking water at major retail outlets.

tn.headline: Tunisian government reviews 2027 economic balance
tn.body: Prime Minister Sara Zaafrani Zenzri presided over a ministerial council on Aug. 19 to examine the draft economic balance for 2027. The document serves as the primary orientation for the country's economic policy.
tn.why: The project establishes the fiscal and economic priorities that will govern state spending and business planning for 2027.

zm.headline: US and Serbia congratulate President-elect Hichilema on re-election
zm.body: The United States and Serbia issued congratulations to President-elect Hakainde Hichilema following the August 15 general election. Both nations pledged to strengthen bilateral relations and cooperation with Zambia. The US welcomed Hichilema's return to office.
zm.why: The pledges aim to maintain diplomatic cooperation and bilateral ties between Zambia and these two nations.

zm.headline: Zambian government mourns former Minister Mutotwe Kafwaya
zm.body: Secretary to the Cabinet Patrick Kangwa expressed regret over the death of former Minister of Works and Transport Mutotwe Kafwaya on Wednesday. The government stated it will make no further comments while law enforcement agencies investigate the matter. Kangwa also condemned threats made against the President.
zm.why: Law enforcement agencies are currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the former minister's death.

zm.headline: Police probe death of 25-year-old woman
zm.body: The Zambia Police Service is investigating the death of 25-year-old Lisa Mutambo, who was brought to a hospital on August 20. Deputy Police Public Relations Officer Chipo Kaitisha reported the incident occurred between 03:30 and 04:30 hours. Police stated no physical injuries were found on the body.
zm.why: The investigation seeks to determine the cause of death following reports that the woman became unconscious after vomiting.

zm.headline: Busoli Royal Establishment recognizes Hichilema's election victory
zm.body: The Busoli Royal Establishment in Chongwe district congratulated President Hakainde Hichilema on his victory in the August 13, 2026, general elections. Representative Prince Kabwata stated the victory represents a renewed mandate from the people. The announcement was made in Chongwe.
zm.why: The recognition by the royal establishment signals traditional leadership support for the president's new term.

eh.headline: Morocco threatens to review Spanish contracts over 2030 World Cup
eh.body: Morocco warned it may review future contracts with Spanish companies if political pressure to exclude Morocco from the 2030 World Cup continues. The warning was reported by Moroccan media.
eh.why: Spanish firms face potential loss of contracts if political boycotts of the joint tournament hosting continue.

ls.headline: Auditor-General calls M30 million budget insufficient
ls.body: The Office of the Auditor-General (OAG) reported a M30 million budget allocation for the 2026/27 financial year. The OAG told the parliamentary Economic and Development Cluster Committee that the funds are insufficient to meet operational needs.
ls.why: The funding gap has left the institution struggling with mounting debts.

ls.headline: LAA and LHDA settle ground rent dispute for M121 million
ls.body: The Land Administration Authority and the Lesotho Highlands Development Authority agreed to a M121 million settlement. The agreement was presented before Chief Justice Sakoane Sakoane to resolve a long-running dispute over unpaid ground rent.
ls.why: The settlement ends a legal conflict between the two state entities over land payments.

ls.headline: Auditor-General spends M12 million on LEC forensic audit
ls.body: The Office of the Auditor-General spent M12 million on a forensic audit of the Lesotho Electricity Company. The expenditure was disclosed during a review by the Economic and Development Cluster this week.
ls.why: The audit seeks to identify financial mismanagement and procurement irregularities at the utility company.

ls.headline: Police sued for M3.2 million over alleged torture
ls.body: Retired government employee Molebatsi Monese is suing Chief Police Advocate Borotho Matsoso for M3.2 million. Monese claims police officers suffocated and electrocuted him during an interrogation.
ls.why: The lawsuit alleges the plaintiff lost two teeth during the police interrogation.

ls.headline: Tsoelopele Investment sues WASCO over M25 million contract
ls.body: Tsoelopele Investment Holdings (Pty) Ltd has petitioned the Commercial Division of the court over a M25 million contract. The contractor alleges the Water and Sewerage Company and the Ministry of Natural Resources reneged on a 2018 appointment.
